case_title: Baldev Singh v. State of Punjab
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302, s.364, s.452 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, who were police personnel, were alleged to have abducted seven members of the complainant's family during a raid on their house. The complainant and his relatives claimed that the abducted individuals were later seen in various police stations and a residential area near a police station. The complainant initially delayed reporting the incident due to fear of retaliation, as one of the accused was a senior police officer. The trial court convicted the accused under sections 302, 364, and 452 of the IPC, while the High Court upheld the conviction. The Supreme Court, however, set aside the murder conviction but maintained the conviction for abduction, directing that the sentence for each of the seven abduction offences should run consecutively.
